**A CLI's prompt, read off the pane and offered as controls**

work-unit · 2026-09-04

the decision it implements: [MUS-D-0142](../decisions.md#mus-d-0142)

what it is written against: [MUS-F-0083](../findings.md#mus-f-0083)

where it renders: [MUS-Q-0075](../questions.md#mus-q-0075)

## Context

MUS-D-0142: the session surface reads a selection prompt off the pane and offers what the screen says is available, driven by the legend the CLI prints rather than by knowledge of the dialog.

**Built so far, and independent of where it renders.** `ReadPrompt` takes a captured screen and returns a title, the description unwrapped, the numbered rows with which one the cursor is on, and the legend — each key and what the CLI says it does. It returns nothing when it cannot read, which is the case the design rests on: no legend means no controls and the terminal is untouched.

**Written against a real capture.** `testdata/prompt-model-picker.txt` is 2,287 bytes taken from a running pane by opening the model picker and dismissing it, escapes and all. Two defects came straight out of that fixture and would not have come out of a remembered format: an empty line read as a box rule, so the title and description were never looked at; and the title taken from the nearest line above the options, which on a wrapped description is its last line.

**Not built.** Where the prompt appears is MUS-Q-0075. Sending a legend key that is a single character rather than a name — `s` in the captured picker — needs a literal send beside the named allowlist, and is the next thing after that answer.

## Status

built

## Where

internal/session/prompt.go, internal/session/testdata/prompt-model-picker.txt

## Evidence

TestThePromptIsAPopUpThatMinimisesIntoTheKeyRow holds the markup and the client: hidden on arrival, drawn after the terminal, held above the dock, capped in height, rebuilt only on change, staying minimised across a redraw, and sending the same key frame the row does. TestThePromptSurvivesTheChromeSplit shows why the frame reads the raw capture: SplitChrome takes the legend off with the rest of the CLI's furniture. TestALegendCharacterArrivesLiterally sends 's' then '3' into a real pane and reads back 's3' on one line.
